# nixidy

> nixidy manages Kubernetes clusters with Nix and the NixOS module system. Applications are configured as Nix modules and rendered to plain YAML manifests, which are committed to a Git repository for Argo CD to deploy (the rendered manifests pattern), or applied to a cluster directly with `nixidy apply`.

Key concepts:

- Environments are defined in a flake with `nixidy.lib.mkEnvs` (or `nixidy.lib.mkEnv` for a single one), each made from a list of modules, and built with `nixidy build .#<env>`.
- An application is `applications.<name>`, with a `namespace` and its resources. Every application gets an Argo CD `Application`, collected in an app-of-apps.
- Resources are typed options under `applications.<name>.resources.<group>.<version>.<kind>.<name>`, also available by their plural kind in camelCase, e.g. `resources.deployments.nginx`. Options for CRDs can be generated with `fromCRD`, `fromCRDModule` and related functions.
- Helm charts (`applications.<name>.helm.releases.<name>`) and Kustomize applications (`applications.<name>.kustomize.applications.<name>`) are rendered as part of an application, and the resources they produce can be overridden like any other resource.
- The rendered output has one directory per application with one file per resource, e.g. `demo/Deployment-nginx.yaml`, and the Argo CD applications in `apps/`.

## Docs

- [Getting Started](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/getting_started/): Set up a project with a flake, define an environment and an application, build it and deploy it with Argo CD
- [Using Helm Charts](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/helm_charts/): Render Helm charts as part of an application and patch the resources they produce
- [Typed Resource Options](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/typed_resources/): The typed resource options, including YAML in an application, and generating options from CRDs with fromCRD/fromChartCRD (generated file), fromCRDModule/fromChartCRDModule (module value, no file) and crdObjects/crdObjectsFromChart (raw CRD manifests)
- [Templates](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/templates/): Define reusable templates with their own options that produce resources
- [Git Strategies](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/git_strategies/): Structure environments as a monorepo, as environment branches or as separate repositories
- [GitHub Actions](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/github_actions/): Build environments and push the rendered manifests from CI with the `arnarg/nixidy/actions/build` and `arnarg/nixidy/actions/switch` actions
- [Transformers](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/transformers/): Functions modifying the manifests rendered by Helm releases and Kustomize applications before nixidy parses them into resources
- [Object Transforms](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/object_transforms/): Declarative rules matching objects, or parts of them, across all applications and updating or replacing them
- [Post-processing](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/postprocessing/): Commands filtering rendered files when an environment is applied, e.g. to encrypt secrets
- [Using nixhelm](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/using_nixhelm/): Use the Helm charts packaged by nixhelm
- [Directly Apply Manifests](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/direct_apply/): Apply an environment to a cluster with `nixidy apply`, using `kubectl apply --prune`, without Argo CD
- [Assertions & Warnings](https://nixidy.dev/user_guide/assertions/): Build-time assertions and warnings, and the built-in validation of references between resources

## Reference

- [CLI Reference](https://nixidy.dev/cli_reference/): Every `nixidy` command and its options: apply, bootstrap, build, diff, info, resources and switch
- [Library Functions](https://nixidy.dev/library/): The `lib.helm`, `lib.kustomize` and `lib.kube` functions available in modules, e.g. `lib.helm.downloadHelmChart`
- [Configuration Options](https://nixidy.dev/options/): All options except the resource options, i.e. `nixidy.*`, `applications.<name>.*` and `templates.*`. Browse the resource options with `nixidy resources <env> [path]`, e.g. `nixidy resources .#prod deployments.spec`

## Optional

- [Architecture Guide](https://nixidy.dev/developer_guide/architecture/): How nixidy is implemented, for contributors
- [arnarg/cluster](https://github.com/arnarg/cluster): A real-world cluster configured with nixidy
- [README](https://github.com/arnarg/nixidy#readme): Project overview with a quick start and examples of the main features
- [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/arnarg/nixidy/discussions): Questions and community support
